tips.title: Precision Blade Angle for Knife Bevels
tips.text: Use a 15-18 degree bevel angle for model cutting blades to achieve optimal edge retention and minimize chipping during intricate cuts. Set the blade at this angle using a precision angle block and test with a straight edge for accuracy.

tips.title: Crosscut Slicing with Coping Saw
tips.text: For clean crosscuts in thin model stock, use a coping saw with a 10-12 tooth per inch blade. Slice the saw blade at 45 degrees relative to the stock to reduce friction and achieve a smoother, more accurate cut.

tips.title: File Direction for Surface Smoothing
tips.text: Always file in one direction along the grain of the model material to avoid creating a 'washboard' effect. Use a medium-cut file (100-220 grit) for initial shaping and a finer cut file (320-600 grit) for final surface refinement.

tips.title: Progressive Sanding with Wet Dry Paper
tips.text: Start with 400 grit wet dry paper for initial sanding, then progress to 1000 grit for smoothing, and finish with 2000 grit for a polished surface. Use a wet sanding technique with water to reduce dust and enhance surface finish.

tips.title: Tool Maintenance with Blade Sharpening Stones
tips.text: Maintain saw blades and knife edges using a 1000-3000 grit diamond stone. Hold the blade at a 15-20 degree angle and perform a 10-minute sharpening cycle with consistent pressure to restore edge geometry and cutting performance.
